foundations.title: Google Consent Mode v2 default-deny + banner
foundations.why: No page sets a consent default; GA4 currently loads unconditionally. New behavioural events must respect consent.
foundations.change: Before gtag('config'): gtag('consent','default',{analytics_storage:'denied',ad_storage:'denied',ad_user_data:'denied',ad_personalization:'denied'}); update to 'granted' on opt-in. trackEvent() becomes a no-op for custom behavioural events until consent is granted.

foundations.title: Pseudonymous unit id for experiments
foundations.why: Experiments need consistent assignment across visits without collecting personal data.
foundations.change: auth.js: const anonId = localStorage.qb_anon_id || (localStorage.qb_anon_id = crypto.randomUUID()); gtag('set','user_properties',{qb_anon_id_hash: <first 8 hex of FNV hash>}). Never send email/username. Only created after consent.

foundations.title: game_session_id on every game event
foundations.why: Without it, starts, abandons and completions cannot be joined into per-game funnels.
foundations.change: Generate crypto.randomUUID() at game start; include in all game/question events.

foundations.title: Register event params as GA4 custom dimensions
foundations.why: The Data API cannot group by event params until they are registered (Admin > Custom definitions). Today none appear to be registered.
foundations.change: Register: game, difficulty, category, opponent_type, phase, end_reason, wait_type, action, experiment_id, variant. Keep question_id OUT of GA4 dimensions (cardinality); send per-question data to the server instead.

foundations.title: Server-side game_events table
foundations.why: Question-level analysis needs exact, unsampled, high-cardinality data that GA4 thresholds and aggregates away.
foundations.change: SQLite table game_events(id, ts, anon_id, game_session_id, event, question_id, props JSON). POST /api/events (batched, consent-gated, rate-limited). Matches the existing better-sqlite3 stack.

foundations.title: experiment_exposure event
foundations.why: Analysis must count only units that actually saw the variant.
foundations.change: trackEvent('experiment_exposure', { experiment_id, variant }) the first time a flagged code path runs per anon_id.

hypotheses.title: Dead waiting time in bot battles
hypotheses.observation: After a wrong or imperfect submission in tech/IB bot battles, the player must wait for the bot's simulated finish (up to ~4 minutes on hard) with nothing to do. Matchmaking falls back to bots after 3s, so this likely affects most battles.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Players who finish before the bot leave during the non-interactive wait, lowering battle completion and replay.
hypotheses.intervention: When the human has finished, resolve the bot's (already simulated) result immediately and show the result screen. Outcome probabilities are unchanged.
hypotheses.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

hypotheses.title: Unclear next step after a game
hypotheses.observation: Result screens offer several equally weighted actions (and a sign-up block for guests above them). Whether players start another game is not measured.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Players finish one game and leave because the next game is not the obvious, one-tap default.
hypotheses.intervention: After measuring post_game_action, test a single primary "Play again" CTA, with sign-up moved below for guests.
hypotheses.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

hypotheses.title: Mobile friction in core game loops
hypotheses.observation: Funnel conversion is significantly lower on mobile than on other devices.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Input-heavy screens (code editor, numeric entry with live check) are harder on touch keyboards, so mobile players abandon more.
hypotheses.intervention: Instrument per-question first-input time on mobile; then test a numeric keypad (inputmode="decimal") and hide code battles on small screens.
hypotheses.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

hypotheses.title: Quant Battle is long and its blitz never ends early
hypotheses.observation: A Quant Battle is a fixed 120s blitz followed by up to 8-12 minutes for four tactical questions (worst case 10-14 minutes).
hypotheses.hypothesis: The match length exceeds what casual visitors budget for, so a share leave before the result screen, especially on mobile.
hypotheses.intervention: Test a shorter format (e.g. 60s blitz and a 6-minute tactical cap) once duration data shows how often players run to the limit.
hypotheses.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

hypotheses.title: Ambiguous answer format in numeric questions
hypotheses.observation: Several numeric questions expect a rounded decimal (or a specific unit) without saying so; tolerance-based grading can then reject correct reasoning.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Players who get a "wrong" verdict on a correct-but-differently-formatted answer feel cheated and abandon the game or stop trusting the bank.
hypotheses.intervention: Show reviewed, clarified wording (explicit unit and rounding) for the flagged questions.
hypotheses.causalStatus: untested: supported by code inspection and correlational data only

experiments.title: Resolve bot battles as soon as the player is done

hypothesis.statement: Removing the non-interactive wait for the bot's simulated finish (up to 85/140/230s by difficulty) will increase the share of players whose bot battles reach the result screen.

variants.description: Current behaviour: after a wrong (single-question) or imperfect (multi-question) submission, the player waits until the bot's scheduled finish time.

As soon as the player has submitted their final answer, the bot's result is drawn immediately from the same accuracy distribution (BOT_ACCURACY) and the result screen is shown. Win/loss probabilities are unchanged; only the wait is removed. Quant Battle is not affected.

primaryMetric.definition: Share of exposed units whose bot battles all reached the result screen (no game_abandoned with opponent_type=bot).

guardrails.definition: Share of exposed units with a game_abandoned before their first submission in any game.

evaluationPlan: Analyse only units with an experiment_exposure event (intent-to-treat from first exposure).
Daily: sample-ratio-mismatch check (chi-square, p < 0.001 pauses the experiment).
Daily: guardrails via always-valid mSPRT p-values; any significant harm recommends revert immediately.
Primary metric is not interpreted before 14 days and 167 units per arm.
After that, stop when the always-valid p < 0.05, or at 665 units per arm / 42 days, whichever first; reaching the cap without significance is "inconclusive".
Report effect size with confidence interval, not just significance. A human makes the final keep/revert decision.
codeChangeOutline: server/index.js startBotMatch: keep the bot resolution in a named function; in the treatment arm call it (and clear the pending timers) from submit_answer once the human has finished.

match_found payload: include { experiment_id, variant } so the client can fire experiment_exposure once.
Default to control whenever the experiment is not live (unapproved, edited after approval, or missing anonId).
risks: Faster losses might feel abrupt; watch premature_exit_rate.
The bot's "thinking" status messages no longer appear in treatment.
